Boston Housing: A Survey of Predictive Models

Authors

Nick Polson

Vadim Sokolov

Introduction

The Boston housing dataset contains 506 census tracts from the 1970 Boston metropolitan area. Each observation records 13 neighborhood characteristics alongside medv, the median home value in thousands of dollars. The goal here is straightforward: compare a range of predictive models for medv, from simple linear regression to neural networks, and assess each on a held-out test set.

The dataset ships with the MASS package. Variables include crime rate (crim), residential zoning (zn), industrial proportion (indus), Charles River adjacency (chas), nitric oxide concentration (nox), average rooms per dwelling (rm), age of units (age), employment distance (dis), highway accessibility (rad), tax rate (tax), pupil-teacher ratio (ptratio), Black population index (black), lower-status population percentage (lstat), and median home value (medv).

Evaluation Metrics

Code 
metrics <- function(yhat, y) {
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((yhat - y)^2))
  mape <- mean(abs((yhat - y) / y)) * 100
  ss_res <- sum((y - yhat)^2)
  ss_tot <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  r2 <- 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
  c(RMSE = round(rmse, 3), MAPE = round(mape, 3), R2 = round(r2, 3))
}

Linear Regression

Four specifications in increasing complexity.

Code 
fit_simple <- lm(medv ~ lstat, data = train)
yhat_simple <- predict(fit_simple, test)
m_simple <- metrics(yhat_simple, test$medv)
Code 
fit_loglog <- lm(log(medv) ~ log(lstat), data = train)
yhat_loglog <- exp(predict(fit_loglog, test))
m_loglog <- metrics(yhat_loglog, test$medv)
Code 
fit_loglin <- lm(log(medv) ~ lstat, data = train)
yhat_loglin <- exp(predict(fit_loglin, test))
m_loglin <- metrics(yhat_loglin, test$medv)
Code 
fit_multi <- lm(log(medv) ~ crim + chas + nox + rm + dis + ptratio + rad + black + log(lstat),
                data = train)
yhat_multi <- exp(predict(fit_multi, test))
m_multi <- metrics(yhat_multi, test$medv)

Ridge and Lasso

Code 
X_train <- model.matrix(medv ~ ., train)[, -1]
y_train <- train$medv
X_test  <- model.matrix(medv ~ ., test)[, -1]
y_test  <- test$medv

lambdas <- 10^seq(2.5, -2, length.out = 100)

Ridge

Code 
fit_ridge <- glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = 0, lambda = lambdas)

coef_ridge <- as.matrix(coef(fit_ridge))[-1, ]
df_ridge <- as.data.frame(t(coef_ridge))
df_ridge$log_lambda <- log(lambdas)
df_long_ridge <- reshape(df_ridge,
  varying   = colnames(df_ridge)[colnames(df_ridge) != "log_lambda"],
  v.names   = "coef",
  timevar   = "variable",
  times     = colnames(df_ridge)[colnames(df_ridge) != "log_lambda"],
  direction = "long"
)
Code 
ggplot(df_long_ridge, aes(x = log_lambda, y = coef, color = variable)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "log(lambda)", y = "Coefficient", title = "Ridge paths") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 6))
Code 
rmse_ridge <- apply(predict(fit_ridge, X_test), 2,
                    function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_test)^2)))
best_ridge  <- lambdas[which.min(rmse_ridge)]
yhat_ridge  <- predict(fit_ridge, X_test, s = best_ridge)
m_ridge <- metrics(yhat_ridge, y_test)

KNN

Code 
ks <- c(2, 10, 20, 50, 100, 300)
knn_results <- lapply(ks, function(k) {
  fit <- kknn(medv ~ ., train = train, test = test, k = k)
  list(k = k, yhat = fit$fitted.values, m = metrics(fit$fitted.values, test$medv))
})
Code 
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))
for (res in knn_results) {
  plot(test$medv, res$yhat, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "steelblue",
       xlab = "Actual", ylab = "Fitted",
       main = paste0("k = ", res$k, "  RMSE = ", res$m["RMSE"]))
  abline(0, 1, col = "red")
}
Code 
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
Code 
knn_rmse <- sapply(knn_results, function(r) r$m["RMSE"])
knn_k    <- sapply(knn_results, function(r) r$k)
plot(log(1 / knn_k), knn_rmse, type = "b", pch = 16, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "log(1/k)  (model complexity)", ylab = "Test RMSE",
     main = "KNN complexity curve")
Code 
best_k   <- knn_results[[which.min(knn_rmse)]]$k
fit_knn  <- kknn(medv ~ ., train = train, test = test, k = best_k)
m_knn <- metrics(fit_knn$fitted.values, test$medv)

Tree Models

Single Tree: medv ~ lstat

Code 
big_tree1 <- tree(medv ~ lstat, data = train, mindev = 0.0001)
pruned1   <- prune.tree(big_tree1, best = 7)
plot(pruned1)
text(pruned1, cex = 0.7)
Code 
lstat_seq <- seq(min(train$lstat), max(train$lstat), length.out = 200)
pred_seq  <- predict(pruned1, data.frame(lstat = lstat_seq))
plot(train$lstat, train$medv, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = "gray50",
     xlab = "lstat", ylab = "medv", main = "Pruned tree fit")
lines(lstat_seq, pred_seq, col = "red", lwd = 2)

2D Tree: medv ~ lstat + dis

Code 
big_tree2 <- tree(medv ~ lstat + dis, data = train, mindev = 0.0001)
pruned2   <- prune.tree(big_tree2, best = 7)
plot(pruned2)
text(pruned2, cex = 0.7)
Code 
lstat_g <- seq(min(train$lstat), max(train$lstat), length.out = 40)
dis_g   <- seq(min(train$dis),   max(train$dis),   length.out = 40)
grid    <- expand.grid(lstat = lstat_g, dis = dis_g)
grid$z  <- predict(pruned2, grid)
z_mat   <- matrix(grid$z, 40, 40)
persp(lstat_g, dis_g, z_mat, theta = 30, phi = 20,
      xlab = "lstat", ylab = "dis", zlab = "medv",
      main = "Tree surface: medv ~ lstat + dis", col = "lightblue")

Full Tree with Cross-Validation

Code 
big_tree_full <- tree(medv ~ ., data = train, mindev = 0.0001)
cv_tree  <- cv.tree(big_tree_full)
best_sz  <- cv_tree$size[which.min(cv_tree$dev)]
pruned_full <- prune.tree(big_tree_full, best = best_sz)
yhat_tree   <- predict(pruned_full, test)
m_tree <- metrics(yhat_tree, test$medv)
Code 
plot(cv_tree$size, cv_tree$dev, type = "b", pch = 16, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Tree size", ylab = "CV deviance")
abline(v = best_sz, col = "red", lty = 2)

SVM

Binary target: medv > 25.

Code 
dat_svm <- Boston
dat_svm$high <- factor(ifelse(dat_svm$medv > 25, "high", "low"))
train_svm <- dat_svm[idx, ]
test_svm  <- dat_svm[-idx, ]

train_svm <- train_svm[, names(train_svm) != "medv"]
test_svm  <- test_svm[,  names(test_svm)  != "medv"]

fit_svm <- svm(high ~ ., data = train_svm, kernel = "radial",
               cost = 1, scale = TRUE)
pred_svm <- predict(fit_svm, test_svm)
acc_svm  <- mean(pred_svm == test_svm$high)
Code 
plot(fit_svm, train_svm, rm ~ lstat)

Logistic Regression

Binary

Code 
train_bin <- train
train_bin$high <- ifelse(train$medv > 25, 1, 0)
test_bin  <- test
test_bin$high  <- ifelse(test$medv  > 25, 1, 0)

fit_glm <- glm(high ~ . - medv, data = train_bin, family = binomial)
pred_glm_prob <- predict(fit_glm, test_bin, type = "response")
pred_glm_cls  <- ifelse(pred_glm_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)
acc_glm <- mean(pred_glm_cls == test_bin$high)

Multinomial

Three classes: low (\(\leq 17\)), medium (\(17 < \text{medv} \leq 25\)), high (\(> 25\)).

Code 
train_multi <- train
train_multi$cls <- cut(train$medv, breaks = c(-Inf, 17, 25, Inf),
                       labels = c("low", "medium", "high"))

test_multi <- test
test_multi$cls <- cut(test$medv, breaks = c(-Inf, 17, 25, Inf),
                      labels = c("low", "medium", "high"))

fit_multi_cls <- multinom(cls ~ . - medv, data = train_multi, trace = FALSE)
pred_multi    <- predict(fit_multi_cls, test_multi)
acc_multi     <- mean(pred_multi == test_multi$cls)

Neural Network

Code 
library(keras)

X_nn  <- scale(X_train)
X_ts  <- scale(X_test,
               center = attr(X_nn, "scaled:center"),
               scale  = attr(X_nn, "scaled:scale"))
y_nn  <- y_train
y_ts  <- y_test

model <- keras_model_sequential() |>
  layer_dense(64, activation = "relu", input_shape = ncol(X_nn)) |>
  layer_dense(64, activation = "relu") |>
  layer_dense(32, activation = "relu") |>
  layer_dense(1)

model |> compile(
  loss      = "mse",
  optimizer = optimizer_rmsprop()
)

history <- model |> fit(
  X_nn, y_nn,
  epochs          = 20,
  batch_size      = 32,
  validation_split = 0.1,
  verbose         = 0
)

yhat_nn <- as.vector(predict(model, X_ts))
m_nn <- metrics(yhat_nn, y_ts)

The network uses two hidden layers of 64 units each, followed by a 32-unit layer, all with ReLU activations. Training uses MSE loss and RMSprop for 20 epochs with a 10% validation split. The architecture is intentionally small to avoid overfitting on 400 training observations.

PLS and PLS + Random Forest

Code 
fit_pls <- plsr(medv ~ ., data = train, ncomp = 10, validation = "CV")
ncomp_opt <- which.min(RMSEP(fit_pls)$val[1, 1, -1])
yhat_pls  <- predict(fit_pls, test, ncomp = ncomp_opt)
m_pls <- metrics(as.vector(yhat_pls), test$medv)
Code 
pls_scores_train <- scores(fit_pls)[, 1:ncomp_opt]
pls_scores_test  <- predict(fit_pls, test, type = "scores")[, 1:ncomp_opt]

df_pls_train <- data.frame(pls_scores_train, medv = train$medv)
df_pls_test  <- data.frame(pls_scores_test)
names(df_pls_test) <- names(df_pls_train)[-ncol(df_pls_train)]

set.seed(42)
fit_pls_rf <- randomForest(medv ~ ., data = df_pls_train)
yhat_pls_rf <- predict(fit_pls_rf, df_pls_test)
m_pls_rf <- metrics(yhat_pls_rf, test$medv)
Code 
plot(RMSEP(fit_pls), legendpos = "topright", main = "PLS CV: RMSEP vs components")
abline(v = ncomp_opt, col = "red", lty = 2)

Summary

Code 
results <- rbind(
  "Linear: simple"              = m_simple,
  "Linear: log-log"             = m_loglog,
  "Linear: log-linear"          = m_loglin,
  "Linear: multiple log-linear" = m_multi,
  "Ridge (best lambda)"         = m_ridge,
  "Lasso (best lambda)"         = m_lasso,
  "KNN"                         = m_knn,
  "Tree (pruned, CV)"           = m_tree,
  "Random Forest (mtry=13)"     = m_rf13,
  "Random Forest (mtry=6)"      = m_rf6,
  "GBM (shrinkage=0.01)"        = m_gbm,
  "GBM (shrinkage=0.2)"         = m_gbm2,
  "PLS"                         = m_pls,
  "PLS + Random Forest"         = m_pls_rf
)
rownames(results)[7] <- paste0("KNN (k=", best_k, ")")

kable(as.data.frame(results),
      caption = "Test-set performance: all models",
      digits  = 3)
Test-set performance: all models
RMSE MAPE R2

Linear: log-log 5.543 17.223 0.701
Linear: log-linear 6.464 17.316 0.593
Linear: multiple log-linear 4.328 13.653 0.818
Ridge (best lambda) 4.790 16.042 0.777
Lasso (best lambda) 4.797 15.996 0.776
KNN (k=2) 4.629 13.078 0.791
Tree (pruned, CV) 4.362 17.840 0.815
Random Forest (mtry=13) 2.848 10.568 0.921
Random Forest (mtry=6) 3.247 10.741 0.897
GBM (shrinkage=0.01) 3.752 12.105 0.863
GBM (shrinkage=0.2) 3.244 12.334 0.898
PLS 5.145 15.958 0.742
PLS + Random Forest 4.879 14.660 0.768

The ensemble methods (random forest and boosting) consistently achieve the lowest RMSE on held-out data. Linear models with log transformation of the outcome reduce skewness and improve over the simple specification. KNN with small \(k\) overfits; the optimal \(k\) is typically in the range 10–50 for this dataset. Regularization via ridge or lasso provides modest improvements over ordinary least squares on this moderately sized dataset.
